## Purpose

This procedure describes the open-vessel, hot-plate acid digestion of
soil, sediment, and sludge samples for near-total extraction of lead
(Pb) and other trace metals, following US EPA Method 3050B [@epa3050b].
The digested extract can be analyzed by ICP-OES, ICP-MS, or flame/
graphite furnace AAS. This is a near-total-dissolution method;
silicates and some refractory oxides are not fully dissolved, but
environmentally available metals are recovered.

For microwave-assisted digestion using the MARS 5 system, see
[SOP-L411](SOP-L411-mars-microwave-digestion.qmd). The microwave method
is faster but processes fewer samples per batch; the hot-plate method
described here is slower but requires only standard fume-hood equipment.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Soils, sediments, and sludge samples requiring trace
  metal analysis (Pb, Cd, Cu, Zn, Cr, As, Ni, Fe, Mn, and others),
  including urban soil lead surveys and photovoltaic panel site
  characterizations
- **Does not apply to:** Water samples (direct acidification or
  separate digestion); samples requiring total silicate dissolution
  (HF-based methods); microwave digestion (see
  [SOP-L411](SOP-L411-mars-microwave-digestion.qmd))
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve SOP, ensure training compliance     |
| Lab Manager       | Maintain equipment, stock reagents          |
| Trained Personnel | Perform digestion per this SOP              |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use; supervised for first digestion |

## Definitions

- **Aqua regia:** A 3:1 (v/v) mixture of HCl and HNO~3~; dissolves noble metals (gold, platinum) and many sulfide minerals not attacked by HNO~3~ alone; more aggressive than single-acid digestion but rarely necessary for soil and sediment.
- **Certified reference material (CRM):** A soil or sediment with certified elemental concentrations from an accredited producer (NIST, USGS); run alongside every digestion batch to verify accuracy.
- **Digestion blank (method blank):** A vessel containing only acid reagents and no soil, processed through the entire digestion procedure; detects contamination from acids, vessels, or the hot plate environment.
- **EPA Method 3050B:** The US EPA hot-plate acid digestion procedure for soils, sediments, and sludges; uses repeated refluxes with HNO~3~ and H~2~O~2~ to dissolve environmentally available trace metals; the reference method for this SOP.
- **Matrix spike:** A sample to which a known concentration of analyte has been added before digestion; used to assess matrix-specific recovery and method accuracy.
- **Partial digestion:** Dissolution of the environmentally available or acid-soluble metal fraction of a sample (EPA 3050B); does not dissolve silicate minerals; appropriate for assessing bioavailability and regulatory compliance; distinguished from total digestion (which requires HF).
- **Reflux:** Heating an acid-sample mixture such that acid vapors condense and return to the vessel; increases digestion efficiency for resistant matrices.


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-danger}
### Critical Safety Warning

This procedure uses concentrated mineral acids (HNO~3~, HCl) and
hydrogen peroxide (H~2~O~2~) at elevated temperatures in open vessels.
All acid handling and digestion must be performed in a certified
chemical fume hood.
:::

### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Concentrated HNO~3~ (15.8 M) is a severe oxidizer and
  corrosive. Concentrated HCl (12 M) is severely corrosive. 30%
  H~2~O~2~ is a reactive oxidizer that can cause exothermic reactions
  with organic matter.
- **Physical:** Hot plate operates at approximately 95 C; digestion
  vessels and watch glasses are hot. Burns from contact with heated
  glassware or splashing acid.
- **Inhalation:** HNO~3~ digestion produces toxic NO~x~ fumes.
  HCl produces irritating HCl vapor. All heating must occur in the
  fume hood.

### Required PPE

- [ ] Chemical splash goggles or face shield
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Acid-resistant gloves (neoprene or heavy-duty nitrile, long-cuffed)
- [ ] Closed-toed shoes

### Emergency Procedures

For acid splashes to skin or eyes, flush immediately at the eyewash
station or safety shower for at least 15 minutes. For inhalation of
fumes, move to fresh air. For acid spills, neutralize small spills with
sodium bicarbonate; for large spills, evacuate and use the spill kit.
Refer to
[SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).

::: {.callout-important}
Never add water to concentrated acid. Add acid slowly to samples. Never
allow digestion vessels to go to dryness; this can volatilize analytes
and damage vessels.
:::


## Equipment and Materials

### Equipment

| Item                          | Notes                                     |
|:------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| Hot plate with temperature control | Capable of maintaining 95 C; placed inside fume hood |
| Digestion vessels             | Teflon (PFA) beakers, glass beakers, or borosilicate digestion tubes |
| Watch glasses                 | Sized to cover the digestion vessels      |
| Analytical balance (0.001 g)  | See [SOP-L102](SOP-L102-using-balances.qmd) |
| Fume hood                     | Required for all steps involving acid and heating |
| Volumetric flasks (50 mL, Class A) | For final dilution                   |
| Graduated pipettes or dispensers | For acid delivery                      |
| Filter funnels and Whatman No. 41 filter paper | For clarifying digests |
| Tongs or heat-resistant clamps | For handling hot vessels                |

### Reagents

| Reagent                       | Grade / Notes                             |
|:------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| Nitric acid (HNO~3~), concentrated (15.8 M) | Trace Metal grade          |
| Hydrochloric acid (HCl), concentrated (12 M) | Trace Metal grade         |
| Hydrogen peroxide (H~2~O~2~), approximately 30% | ACS reagent grade    |
| Deionized water (Type I)      | From [*SOP-L11*](SOP-L11-milli-q-water.qmd) |

::: {.callout-note}
All reagents must be Trace Metal grade or equivalent. Analyze a reagent
blank before each batch; the blank must read below the method detection
limit (MDL) for all target analytes.
:::


## Procedure

### Sample Preparation

1. Air-dry the soil at room temperature or at 60 C until constant mass
2. Pass through a No. 10 sieve (2 mm) per
   [SOP-F400 Soil Sampling](../field_sops/SOP-F400-soil-sampling.qmd)
3. Homogenize thoroughly using a mortar and pestle
4. Determine gravimetric moisture on a companion subsample per
   [SOP-L400](SOP-L400-soil-moisture.qmd)

### Glassware Cleaning

Acid-wash all vessels, volumetric flasks, and watch glasses per
[SOP-L101 Glassware Cleaning](SOP-L101-glassware-cleaning.qmd),
Section 6.3 (10% HNO~3~ acid bath). Rinse with reagent water and
dry in a clean environment.

### Weighing

1. Weigh 0.50--1.00 g of prepared soil into a clean digestion vessel
2. Record the exact mass to the nearest 0.001 g in the lab notebook

### Initial Nitric Acid Digestion

1. Working in the fume hood, add approximately 10 mL of concentrated
   HNO~3~ to the vessel
2. Cover with a watch glass
3. Place on the hot plate set to approximately 95 C. Do not allow the
   solution to boil.
4. Reflux gently until the initial vigorous reaction subsides and the
   volume begins to reduce. Do not allow the sample to go to dryness.
5. Continue heating for approximately 30--60 minutes, periodically
   lifting the watch glass to rinse the underside with DI water back
   into the vessel

### Oxidation with H~2~O~2~

1. Remove the vessel from the hot plate and allow to cool slightly
2. Add 1--2 mL of 30% H~2~O~2~ dropwise. Wait for effervescence to
   subside between drops.
3. Return to the hot plate and resume heating at 95 C
4. Repeat the H~2~O~2~ additions until the reaction is minimal
   (typically 2--4 additions) and the digest appears light-colored

::: {.callout-warning}
Add H~2~O~2~ very slowly. The reaction with organic matter is
exothermic and can cause violent spattering if added too quickly,
especially to hot solutions. Always cool the vessel first.
:::

### HCl Treatment

1. Add approximately 5 mL of concentrated HCl to the digest
2. Cover and heat at approximately 95 C for 15--30 minutes
3. This step dissolves residual metal precipitates and improves
   recovery of metals such as Fe, Al, and Pb

### Volume Reduction

1. Remove the watch glass and continue heating at approximately 95 C
2. Reduce the volume to approximately 5 mL
3. Monitor closely and do not allow the sample to go to dryness

::: {.callout-important}
Evaporation to dryness will cause loss of volatile analytes (As, Se,
Hg) and can bake residues onto the vessel walls, making quantitative
recovery impossible.
:::

### Dilution and Filtration

1. Remove from the hot plate and allow to cool to room temperature
2. Rinse the vessel walls and watch glass with small portions of
   DI water
3. If undissolved material is present, filter through Whatman No. 41
   filter paper into a clean 50 mL volumetric flask, rinsing the
   filter and vessel quantitatively
4. If the solution is clear, transfer directly to the volumetric flask
5. Bring to 50.0 mL with DI water
6. Mix thoroughly
7. Transfer to a clean, labeled polyethylene or polypropylene storage
   bottle. Store at 4 C until analysis.


## Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

### QC Requirements

- **Method blank:** Include one vessel containing reagents only (no
  soil) in each digestion batch. The blank must read below the MDL for
  all target analytes.
- **Certified reference material (CRM):** Digest a CRM with known
  metal concentrations in each batch. Recovery: 80--120%.
- **Matrix spike:** Spike a duplicate sample with a known concentration
  of the target analyte(s). Recovery: 75--125%.
- **Duplicate digestions:** At least 10% of samples. Relative percent
  difference (RPD) less than 20%.
- **Calibration verification:** Verify with a mid-range check standard
  every 10 samples during instrumental analysis.

### Calculations

**Metal concentration in soil (mg/kg dry weight):**

$$
C_{\text{soil}} = \frac{C_{\text{digest}} \times V_{\text{final}}}{M_{\text{soil}}}
$$

where $C_{\text{digest}}$ = concentration in the digest (mg/L),
$V_{\text{final}}$ = final volume (mL, typically 50), and
$M_{\text{soil}}$ = mass of dried soil (g).

For soil dried at 60 C, apply a moisture correction to report on a
105 C oven-dry basis (see
[SOP-L400](SOP-L400-soil-moisture.qmd)):

$$
C_{\text{soil, OD}} = C_{\text{soil}} \times \frac{100 + \theta_{60}}{100 + \theta_{105}}
$$


## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Disposal Method                          |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Acid digest waste (all liquids from digestion) | Collect in labeled acid waste carboy; EH&S hazardous waste pickup |
| Used filter paper             | Acid waste stream (contaminated with metals and acid) |
| Digested soil residue         | Acid waste carboy                        |
| Spent H~2~O~2~               | Small volumes may go into acid waste; large volumes, consult EH&S |

::: {.callout-warning}
### Acid Waste

All waste from this procedure contains concentrated mineral acids and
dissolved metals. **Do not pour down the drain.** Collect in a labeled
polyethylene carboy for EH&S hazardous waste pickup.
:::


## References

- USEPA. (1996). Method 3050B: Acid digestion of sediments, sludges,
  and soils. Revision 2. In: *Test Methods for Evaluating Solid Waste,

  Agency, Washington, DC.
- APHA, AWWA, WEF. (2012). *Standard Methods for Examination of Water
  and Wastewater*. 22nd ed. American Public Health Association (Eds.).
  Washington. 1360 pp.

::: {#refs}
:::


## Training Record

Before performing hot-plate acid digestion independently, personnel
must:

1. Read this SOP, [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd),
   and [SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd)
   in full
2. Review the SDS for concentrated HNO~3~, HCl, and 30% H~2~O~2~
3. Observe a trained operator perform a complete digestion cycle
4. Perform at least one complete digestion batch under direct
   supervision, including blank and CRM, with acceptable QC results
5. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager


## Appendix A: Example Calculation {.appendix}


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Trace metal concentration from hot-plate digest
# EPA 3050B

C_digest_mg_L <- 1.24      # Pb concentration from ICP-MS (mg/L)
V_final_mL <- 50.0         # Final dilution volume (mL)
M_soil_g <- 0.752           # Mass of dried soil digested (g)

C_soil_mg_kg <- (C_digest_mg_L * V_final_mL) / M_soil_g

cat(sprintf("Digest concentration: %.3f mg/L Pb\n", C_digest_mg_L))
cat(sprintf("Soil mass:           %.3f g\n", M_soil_g))
cat(sprintf("Final volume:        %.1f mL\n", V_final_mL))
cat(sprintf("Soil Pb:             %.1f mg/kg\n", C_soil_mg_kg))

# Screening levels
cat(sprintf("\nCA DTSC residential screening level: 80 mg/kg\n"))
cat(sprintf("EPA RSL residential: 400 mg/kg\n"))
```
:::



## Appendix B: Method Comparison -- Hot Plate vs. Microwave {.appendix}

| Feature                       | Hot Plate (EPA 3050B, this SOP) | Microwave (EPA 3051A, [SOP-L411](SOP-L411-mars-microwave-digestion.qmd)) |
|:------------------------------|:-------------------------------|:--------------------------------------|
| Vessel type                   | Open (reflux under watch glass) | Sealed (pressurized)                 |
| Temperature                   | Approximately 95 C             | 175 C                                |
| Digestion time                | 2--4 hours (hands-on)          | 10 minutes (automated)               |
| Sample throughput             | Limited by hot plate space     | Up to 24 vessels per run              |
| Equipment required            | Hot plate + fume hood          | MARS 5 microwave system              |
| Acid volume per sample        | Approximately 15 mL total      | 10 mL                                |
| Organic matter handling       | H~2~O~2~ oxidation step        | Sealed vessel; pre-digest if vigorous |
| Metal recovery                | Comparable for most elements   | Comparable; slightly higher for volatile elements due to sealed system |
| Best for                      | Small batches; no access to microwave | Routine batches; time-sensitive work |
